text:
Talia: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands on capacity: PMs want a short, copy-pasteable explanation of what happens if US-West prewarm lanes are delayed by procurement. What is the immediate user-visible impact and what fallback order do we use?

Marco: Short version: we try soft mitigations first (quantized variants + smaller batches) to keep p95/p99 latency close to normal. If pressure is sustained, we remap burst/reserved buckets and then consider cross-region failover to US-Central or US-East. Expect temporary p99 jitter: ~100-350ms depending on path.

Asha: For CS/PMs: tagging exists in console (customer -> capacity tags). Use that to tell customers whether they're reserved, prewarm_eligible, or on-demand. I'll export the CSV and drop it in #cs by EOD.

Talia: Can ops drop a tiny runbook snippet we can paste in customer comms?

Devon: Pasteable snippet below (we'll expand into full runbook):
```
# customer-facing fallback summary
if prewarm.unavailable:
  1) route -> quantized_variant (same model family)
  2) reduce_batch_size(timeout=3m)
  3) remap_reserved_buckets(if sustained>=10m)
  4) cross-region-failover(if sustained>=30m)
```

OpsBot: Runbook stub created: https://confluence.redwood/infra/us-west-fallbacks :white_check_mark:

Talia: Perfect  thanks. Action items: Asha to share CSV with CS, Marco to add latency numbers to the roadmap notes, Devon to expand runbook. I'll coordinate customer comms once those are in. :thumbsup:
